analysis:
The supplied units are documentation only: docs/architecture/inference.md (cluster stop ordering, stop-drain token and Qwen27 capacity/MTP prose) and docs/operations/provider-release.md (v0.10.12 to v0.10.13 release-prep text). The supplied evidence contains no code, workflow, key-handling, attestation, authorization, encryption or wire-protocol change, so no concrete security regression is identified.

The inference.md excerpt describes cluster stop semantics: stopped intent retained, no force kill, and the local-only stopDrain token. It also covers restoreStart after an automatic re-plan or approval change, which runs under the command lock and only on a claim the other Mac confirmed. The surrounding text states that normal wire fields and lease deadlines are unchanged. These are descriptive claims. I could not verify them against the Swift sources (ClusterService, OnboardingLive, ClusterService+RestartingStop), which were not supplied. The patch excerpt for inference.md is truncated (the ClusterOnboardingStopped / stopsAsked wire-field text near lines 453-473), so the added stopsAsked reply field and the compare-under-lock behavior were not fully reviewed. Relevant surfaces are TB-002 (coordinator-provider wire contract, ClusterControlReply.stopsAsked optional field) and A-018 (serving availability). A remote or peer-supplied stop count could affect only availability, and that cannot be assessed without the code.

The provider-release.md change shortens release notes and pins. It records that the pins libs/mlx 72dffa2d, mlx-swift b1c94d29 and mlx-swift-lm 44ab1755 are unchanged from v0.10.12, with an expected metallib_hash unchanged. It drops the 'Confirm against the final DevNet build' hedging and the ordered rollout checklist, replacing them with a coordinator snapshot note. The removal of the explicit rollout-order approvals is a process-documentation change, not a control change; the Prerequisites section on explicit human authorization remains in the base text. It does not weaken the signed-tag, ancestry, or release-key controls that are visible. Release identity (A-011, A-017) is not touched. No threat-model update is needed from these docs alone. Remaining question: whether the underlying v0.10.13 code changes (#2040, #2042) in other batches touch trust boundaries.
